bug_description.normalized: The staged 40-byte `config_map_fuzzer` witness is split into three slices. The harness copies bytes 0-14 into `null_terminated1`, where the embedded NUL makes `strlen(k_buf)` at `src/flb_kv.c:71` yield `k_len == 11` and later materialize key `mult_string`; bytes 15-29 are copied into `null_terminated2`, where `strlen(v_buf)` at `src/flb_kv.c:74` yields `v_len == 15` for the SDS later double-freed; the remaining 10 bytes are passed only as a context-name string. Stage 01 reproduced against the prepared fluent-bit checkout at `72b62d2270edda9a0281ff8a6c3903d99e1892c9`, not ARVO metadata's older `2f8374ed...`; this staged tree still contains the vulnerable alias at `src/flb_config_map.c:681` and matches the saved ASan stack. In the first loop iteration, the harness selects `config_map_mult`, so `flb_config_map_set()` matches the attacker-controlled key `mult_string` to a config-map entry with both `FLB_CONFIG_MAP_STR` and `FLB_CONFIG_MAP_MULT`. The vulnerable code stores `entry->val.str = kv->val` instead of duplicating the SDS, so the same heap allocation is owned simultaneously by the property-list node and by the config-map mult-entry list. `flb_config_map_destroy()` frees that shared SDS first through `destroy_map_val()`, and the harness immediately calls `flb_kv_release(&prop)`, whose `flb_kv_item_destroy()` invokes `flb_sds_destroy(kv->val)` on the same pointer. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting second free at `src/flb_sds.c:393`. The fix changes the aliasing assignment to `entry->val.str = flb_sds_create(kv->val)`, so each owner frees its own allocation.

staged_source_snapshot.description: Prepared vulnerable checkout used by Stage 01 reproduction and by this Stage 02 trace.

source.description: First non-harness project statement on the crashing path that consumes attacker bytes into vulnerability-relevant state by converting the first helper buffer into the truncated key length later used to materialize `kv->key` and match the vulnerable `mult_string` config-map entry.
source.value_from: The exact staged witness starts with the 15-byte slice `6d 75 6c 74 5f 73 74 72 69 6e 67 00 20 20 20`. In the helper buffer created from that slice, byte 11 is already `\0`, so this `strlen(k_buf)` stops there and yields `k_len == 11`; the later `flb_sds_create_len()` call therefore materializes the key as `"mult_string"`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This SDS allocation from the second witness slice is the exact heap object later aliased into the config-map entry, freed once by `destroy_map_val`, and freed again at the sanitizer sink.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Witness bytes 15-29 are `20 20 20 20 20 20 20 ff ff ff 20 ff ff 20 ff`. The helper buffer created from that slice appends its own trailing `\0`, but there is no earlier NUL, so `strlen(v_buf)` at `src/flb_kv.c:74` yields `v_len == 15` and this call allocates the 15-byte SDS later double-freed.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The multi-string config-map entry takes raw ownership of `kv->val` instead of duplicating it, so the config-map mult list and the original property list both free the same SDS allocation.
root_cause.note: The fix in `patch.diff` changes this exact line to `entry->val.str = flb_sds_create(kv->val);`, which removes the shared-ownership condition that drives the second free.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. The second `flb_sds_destroy()` call converts the stale SDS pointer back to its header and passes that already-freed allocation to `flb_free()`.

parser_admitted.description: On the first loop iteration `i == 0`, `configs[0] = config_map_mult`, so the exact witness key/value pair reaches `flb_config_map_set()` with a mult-capable map whose `mult_string` entry can own string values.

first_cleanup.description: The saved previous-free stack shows this cleanup runs first and reaches `destroy_map_val()` on the aliased `mult_string` entry.

second_cleanup.description: Immediately after map destruction, the same iteration releases the original property list, sending the still-stored `kv->val` pointer to `flb_kv_item_destroy()` for the second free.

coarse_trace.summary: The exact 40-byte witness is split into a key slice, a value slice, and a context-name tail. In the first loop iteration the harness creates one property and chooses `configs[0] = config_map_mult`.

Property creation uses `strlen` to truncate the first helper buffer to `k_len == 11`, computes `v_len == 15` for the second helper buffer, then materializes `kv->key = "mult_string"` and the 15-byte SDS `kv->val`.
Config-map lookup matches `mult_string`, takes the `FLB_CONFIG_MAP_MULT` string branch, and stores the same `kv->val` pointer in a new `flb_config_map_val` entry instead of duplicating it.
Map destruction walks the mult-entry list and frees the aliased SDS once through `destroy_map_val()`.
Property-list cleanup immediately frees the same SDS again, and AddressSanitizer reports the double-free at `flb_sds_destroy:393`.

fine_trace.note: The harness copies witness bytes 0-14 into a fresh NUL-terminated helper buffer that becomes `k_buf`. Those bytes are `6d 75 6c 74 5f 73 74 72 69 6e 67 00 20 20 20`; because byte 11 is already `\0`, that embedded terminator survives and later truncates the key to `"mult_string"`.

After step 1 advances `data` and `size`, the harness copies witness bytes 15-29 into a second helper buffer that becomes `v_buf` and appends its own trailing `\0`. This 15-byte slice `20 20 20 20 20 20 20 ff ff ff 20 ff ff 20 ff` contains no earlier NUL, so the later string conversion observes the full 15-byte value.

Source. `flb_kv_item_create()` consumes the helper buffer from step 1 as a C string and stops at its embedded NUL, so `k_len` becomes 11. That truncation makes the later key SDS equal to `"mult_string"` instead of the full 15-byte witness slice.
The helper buffer from step 2 has no embedded NUL before its appended terminator, so `v_len` becomes 15. This exact length later sizes the SDS allocation that is double-freed.

Using the truncated `k_len` from step 3, `flb_kv_item_create_len()` copies 11 bytes from `k_buf` and materializes `kv->key` as the SDS `"mult_string"`. This is the key later used for config-map lookup.

Using `v_len == 15` from step 4, this call allocates `kv->val` from the second helper buffer. ASan's allocation stack reaches this site through `flb_sds_create_len()` and `sds_alloc()`, identifying this SDS as the allocation later shared and freed twice.

During the first fuzzer loop iteration, `map` was created from `configs[0] = config_map_mult`, so this comparison eventually matches the copied `m->name` `"mult_string"`. The matched config entry therefore has `m->type == FLB_CONFIG_MAP_STR` and `m->flags & FLB_CONFIG_MAP_MULT`, selecting the vulnerable multi-string population path.

Root cause. For the matched `mult_string` entry, the new `flb_config_map_val` stores the raw `kv->val` pointer instead of duplicating the SDS. The same heap allocation from step 6 is now owned both by the property-list node and by this config-map entry. The fix replaces this alias with `flb_sds_create(kv->val)`.

The aliased `entry` is appended to the `mult_string` list owned by the copied config map. `flb_config_map_create()` already initialized `m->value.mult` for `FLB_CONFIG_MAP_MULT` entries, so `flb_config_map_destroy()` will later walk this list and release `entry->val.str`.

First free. `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` destroys the config map before releasing `prop`, and `flb_config_map_destroy()` iterates the mult-entry list from step 9. For the aliased `mult_string` entry, `destroy_map_val()` passes the shared SDS pointer into `flb_sds_destroy()`, matching ASan's previous-free stack.

After `flb_config_map_destroy(map)` returns, the harness immediately calls `flb_kv_release(&prop)`. `flb_kv_item_destroy()` therefore sends the still-stored pointer from step 6 into `flb_sds_destroy()` a second time.

Sink. The second `flb_sds_destroy()` from step 11 computes the SDS header and frees it here. Because step 10 already freed the same allocation through the aliased config-map entry, AddressSanitizer reports the double-free at this line.

free_context.note: ASan's previous-free stack reports `destroy_map_val -> flb_sds_destroy -> flb_free` during `flb_config_map_destroy(map)`.

allocation_context.note: ASan's allocation stack reaches `flb_sds_create_len()` and `sds_alloc()` through this exact `kv->val` allocation site.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The fix replaces the aliasing assignment `entry->val.str = kv->val` with `entry->val.str = flb_sds_create(kv->val)`, so map cleanup and property cleanup free different SDS allocations.

format.name: fluent-bit config_map_fuzzer 40-byte three-slice property blob
format.contract: Exactly the staged 40-byte witness in `gt_results/arvo_27025/poc`. Under `config_map_fuzzer`, bytes 0-14 are copied to `null_terminated1` and interpreted as `"mult_string\0   "`, so `flb_kv_item_create()` sees key `"mult_string"`. Bytes 15-29 are copied to `null_terminated2` as the exact 15-byte NUL-free value slice `20 20 20 20 20 20 20 ff ff ff 20 ff ff 20 ff`, which becomes the SDS later double-freed. Bytes 30-39 become the trailing context-name string `20 20 ff ff 20 ff ff ff 20 20`; this tail is not needed for the double-free beyond satisfying the exact witnessed file layout. The first loop iteration then uses `configs[0] = config_map_mult`, so the `mult_string` config entry aliases that SDS into `m->value.mult` and the subsequent `flb_config_map_destroy(map)` / `flb_kv_release(&prop)` pair frees it twice.
